newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-ICC BACK TEST WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ICC BACK TEST WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: International Cricket Council (ICC) chief executive David Richards said on Friday that a formally recognised test world championship could be instituted by the end of the year.

Richards told a news conference at the Wanderers on the first day of the first test between South Africa and Australia that he would be seeking assurances from all nine test playing nations that a formalised world championship would have their backing

"The next ICC meeting is in Kuala Lumpur on March 23 and once we've agreed in principle it's just a question of juggling itineraries to make sure that all the countries play each other home and away over, perhaps, a four year period,'' Richards said.
'' The points system suggested by Matthew Engel seems to be the simplest".
Engel, editor of Wisden, cricket's annual almanac, suggested a system whereby a team winning a series would get two points, one point for a draw and no points for a lost series.
Richards added: "There is a feeling that we need to reaffirm what the players feel about the importance and status of test cricket and a world championship would certainly raise its profile.

"The ICC cannot limit the number of one day games played around the world -- that is up to each individual country -- but both Mark Taylor and Hansie Cronje have expressed their concerns to me about the hectic nature of modern playing schedules".
Taylor and Cronje captain Australia and South Africa respectively.
